note: SL-101 review M1 (O-017), closed as a class: the Controlled Folder Access lists the record prints a count of, as Windows PowerShell 5.1 serialises them to JSON. Get-MpPreference hands an ordinary user, in place of the list, one placeholder entry that begins 'N/A:' (measured on this PC at 9851b9c, unelevated: ControlledFolderAccessAllowedApplications was ["N/A: Must be an administrator to view exclusions"], so the survey's '1 allowed app' was never a count of apps). Each row is fed, alone, as the value of BOTH lists (protected, allowed) to DefenderState.Describe. 'expect' is the text the line must carry after 'protected folders=' and 'allowed apps='. 'naive' is what the counting rule the design handed to build (null 0, [] 0, a string 1, an array its length) printed for the same value, so the rows where naive differs from expect are the ones the fix closed (kind placeholder), and every kind real row is one the fix must leave alone.
bounded_by: Who produces the members: only Defender's own cmdlet, for a caller that is not an administrator, and only in the two list properties the record reads (ControlledFolderAccessProtectedFolders, ControlledFolderAccessAllowedApplications). The census of Get-MpPreference on this PC at 9851b9c, unelevated (powershell.exe 5.1, every property whose value begins 'N/A:'): 11 properties carry the placeholder, AttackSurfaceReductionOnlyExclusions, AttackSurfaceReductionRules_RuleSpecificExclusions, AttackSurfaceReductionRules_RuleSpecificExclusions_Id, BruteForceProtectionExclusions, ControlledFolderAccessAllowedApplications, ControlledFolderAccessDefaultProtectedFolders, ExclusionExtension, ExclusionIpAddress, ExclusionPath, ExclusionProcess and RemoteEncryptionProtectionExclusions, and the record reads one of them (ControlledFolderAccessAllowedApplications) beside ControlledFolderAccessProtectedFolders, which read as an empty list here and may carry it once it is not empty. Ten of the eleven say 'N/A: Must be an administrator to view exclusions'; ControlledFolderAccessDefaultProtectedFolders says 'N/A: Must be an administrator to view default protected folders' (row P09), which is why the text after the prefix is not compared. The placeholder is the property's whole value, as a one-element array (measured) or as a bare string (what a different serialiser or a cmdlet that stops wrapping it would give). Its text after the first four characters is Defender's own prose, differs between properties and may be localised or reworded, so the grammar is the 'N/A:' prefix only, compared without case and after leading white space: no Windows path can begin that way, because a colon in a path is only ever the second character after a drive letter, so no real entry is taken for a placeholder. A list that holds a placeholder beside anything else cannot be counted from what is visible, so it reads as hidden too.
